newsitem.title: UK: Shell moves to unify European advertising message.
newsitem.headline: Shell moves to unify European advertising message.

text.p: Shell International Ltd, part of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, on Friday said its decision to consolidate its European advertising with one ad agency is part of an effort to produce greater international consistency for the Shell brand.

Earlier on Friday Shell said it named J. Walter Thompson, part of WPP Group Plc, as its sole strategic and creative advertising agency for all its brand advertising across 30 Western European, Eastern European and Scandanavian countries.
Shell until now had been contracting with advertising agencies on a country-by-country basis in Europe, although some ad agencies have won accounts with Shell in more than one country.

"What we will be able to do now is share campaigns," Julian Barnes, a Shell spokesman, told Reuters in a telephone interview. "It should be more cost efficient, and it should help us with a consistency of message."
Shell, however, may at times use different commercials in various countries to reflect cultural differences, although all its ads will carry a consistent message, Barnes said.
The move to one ad agency follows Shell's naming last year of CIA MediaNetwork to handle all of Shell's media buying across Europe. The relationship with CIA MediaNetwork is unchanged.
Shell said both moves are consistent with its move towards greater integration of its operations in Europe.

Shell expects the total European advertising expenditure to be handled by J. Walter Thompson to be about $80 million to $100 million a year, roughly the same as it is currently spending across Europe, Barnes said.
All of Shell's European companies are expected to be using J. Walter Thompson by the end of 1997, as existing contracts with other ad agencies expire.
